news.headline: Exchanged RSUs Settle: NeurAxis Issues About 592,000 Shares to CEO, CMO and Chief Regulatory Officer
news.summary: Form 4s filed August 26 show shares actually delivered on August 24 under the option-for-RSU exchange: 199,188 to CEO Brian Carrico (227,336 owned after), 199,106 to CMO Adrian Miranda and 193,678 to Chief Regulatory Officer Thomas Carrico, roughly 592,000 shares in total. The exchange cancelled 1,319,394 legacy options in return for an equal number of RSUs that vested immediately, so the issuance converts underwater paper into real share count against roughly 12.6 million shares outstanding as of August 6.

news.headline: NeurAxis 8-K Details Completed Option Exchange Plus New Three-Year Management and Director Equity Grants
news.summary: The option-for-RSU exchange approved by shareholders on June 10 went effective July 24, cancelling 1,319,394 options and issuing an equal number of immediately vesting RSUs. On August 13 the compensation committee added three-year-vesting grants of 193,329 RSUs to Brian Carrico, 141,479 to CFO Timothy Henrichs, 133,341 to Adrian Miranda and 135,906 to Thomas Carrico, plus 127,120 one-time shares to independent directors after a consultant found pay below market.

news.headline: NRXS Stock Dips Post Q2 Earnings Despite Revenue Surge and Gross Margin Gain
news.summary: Shares fell 8.6% in the days after the August 11 print versus a 0.3% gain for the S&P 500, as the wider-than-expected loss outweighed the revenue beat. The review highlighted IB-Stim unit deliveries up 60% year over year, gross margin at 85.9%, traction with two large commercial payers and the first commercial activity in the Veterans Affairs channel.

news.headline: NeurAxis Reports Record Second Quarter 2026 Results: Revenue Up 116%, 100M+ Covered Lives, VA Sales Force Due by September 15
news.summary: Q2 revenue rose 115.7% year over year to $1.93M on 60% unit growth (first-half revenue $3.6M, +98%), with gross margin expanding to 85.9% as the Category I CPT code for PENFS pushed more devices to full reimbursement price; cash was $8.3M at June 30 after raising $2.5M via the ATM and warrant redemptions. On the earnings call management said 24 commercial insurers now carry formal PENFS policies covering 100M+ lives, prior-authorization approvals improved to 31% year to date from 12%, and the company committed to 10 commission-only Veterans Affairs territory reps in the field by September 15, 2026.

news.headline: Resale Prospectus for 1.92 Million Insider and Employee Shares Goes Effective, Adding Potential Supply
news.summary: The S-3 filed July 23 was declared effective August 3 and the final prospectus followed on August 6, registering 1,923,194 shares for resale by selling stockholders - 849,212 already-issued shares, 923,776 underlying RSUs and 150,206 director service shares. That is about 15% of the 12,477,309 shares outstanding as of July 22 and includes stakes held by CEO Brian Carrico (213,445 registered), CFO Timothy Henrichs (231,591) and former director Christopher Brown (792,837).

news.headline: NeurAxis Expands Payer Coverage with New Policies, Adding Over 500,000 Mid-Atlantic Covered Lives
news.summary: NeurAxis announced additional medical policy coverage for PENFS from a regional Mid-Atlantic health plan, adding more than 500,000 covered lives ahead of the Q2 print a week later. The addition was one of the steps management cited on the subsequent earnings call in reaching the 24-insurer, 100M+ covered-lives total reported for Q2.

catalysts.label: VA sales force fully staffed
catalysts.detail: Management committed on the August 11 call to having 10 commission-only (1099) Veterans Affairs territory representatives in the field by September 15, 2026. The VA Federal Supply Schedule contract for IB-Stim has been live since December 1, 2025 and management says VA adoption is already running ahead of initial expectations. This hire is the step that turns the channel from opportunistic orders into a Q4 volume driver, and it is now about two weeks away.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 earnings
catalysts.detail: Next quarterly report, expected around mid-November on the company's usual cadence (Q1 on May 12, Q2 on August 11). Key tests: whether triple-digit revenue growth holds against a tougher comparison, whether ASP keeps climbing from $992 toward the $1,195 list price, how much of the promised H2 opex step-up in sales, marketing, clinical and policy hiring eats into the improving cash burn on an $8.3M cash balance, and the first read on VA rep productivity after the September 15 staffing target.

catalysts.label: Major national payer coverage decision
catalysts.detail: Talks with two large commercial payers gained traction in Q2 and management is cautiously optimistic about a coverage win in H2 2026 or early 2027. The CEO has framed a single large national payer add as the step that could slingshot the company toward profitability, since hospitals generally want roughly 70% of their patient population covered before adopting broadly. Twenty-four commercial insurers currently have formal PENFS policies.

catalysts.label: State Medicaid adoption of CPT 64567
catalysts.detail: Many states have still not added CPT code 64567 to their 2026 fee schedules, leaving no payment methodology and blocking coverage for Medicaid beneficiaries even though the Category I code has been in effect since January 1, 2026. Each state that loads the code onto its schedule unlocks a new reimbursed patient pool, and Medicaid is disproportionately important in pediatric gastroenterology.

catalysts.label: Covered lives above 200 million
catalysts.detail: Management reiterated on the Q2 call that it expects to exceed 200 million covered lives by the end of 2027, roughly doubling from the 100 million-plus reached today, with the CEO saying he would be highly disappointed to miss that level. Reaching it would effectively cover the full serviceable market and requires a steady run of payer-policy wins like the August 4 Mid-Atlantic addition.

pulse: The stock trades around $6.90-6.95 (market cap near $90M) on about 12.6M shares outstanding as of August 6 and rising toward 14M once August's RSU settlements and director grants are fully counted, against $8.3M of cash reported at June 30. Commercial momentum continues to build - a Mid-Atlantic payer added over 500,000 covered lives on August 4, Q2 revenue grew 116% year over year with gross margin near 86%, and 24 insurers now cover 100M+ lives - but shares still sold off after the August 11 print on a wider-than-expected loss, and late August was dominated by dilution-related housekeeping (an effective resale prospectus for 1.92M insider/employee shares and roughly 592,000 exchange RSUs settling to executives). All near-term attention is now on the September 15 deadline for a 10-rep Veterans Affairs sales force to be fully in the field, with two large commercial payers in negotiation, state Medicaid CPT 64567 fee-schedule adoption, and the next earnings print (expected mid-November) as the catalysts to watch into year-end.
